insight.title: How Light Becomes Us
insight.subtitle: The quiet alchemy that connects the sun to our morning coffee.

sections.text: Every morning, a silent wave of golden light travels ninety-three million miles to reach your garden. It feels like a gentle warmth on your skin, but it is actually the fuel for everything you see. Before you even wake up, the world is already hard at work, catching stars.

Green leaves act like tiny, sophisticated solar panels. They drink in this ancient light and turn it into the sugar that builds every branch and blade of grass. It is a slow, elegant transformation where the invisible becomes solid. Life is simply sunlight held together by a little bit of quiet magic.

When you take a bite of an apple or a deep breath of crisp air, you are consuming that stored radiance. We are not separate from the universe; we are part of its endless cycle. Everything we do is powered by a distant star, woven into the very fabric of our daily lives.

news.title: Canadian military members likely involved in planning U.S. strikes on Iran, retired general says
news.description: A retired Canadian major-general says personnel on exchange with U.S. Central Command were likely involved in planning and targeting airstrikes on Iran unless Ottawa explicitly barred participation. As U.S. and Israeli forces intensify their campaign, The Department of National Defence has so far declined to clarify Canada's operational role.

news.title: Vast web of cold gas observed at the heart of the Milky Way
news.description: WASHINGTON: Astronomers have produced the largest and most detailed map ever made of the vast web of cold cosmic gas stretching across the heart of our galaxy, showing thread-like filaments resembling rivers of material flowing through space that sometimes converge into bright clouds where new stars form.
